lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: You are examining a newborn child 1 hour after birth and you check for their red reflex using an ophthalmoscope. You do not find a red reflection in their eyes. Which of the following is the next best step?

options.html: Proceed with your examination. A red reflection should not be seen in the child’s eyes.
Proceed with your examination as this is normal in newborn children. Check the baby for a red reflex 1 month after its birth, at which point it should have developed.

While most children are born with a red reflex, some children will develop this within the first year of life. If it has not been developed then, this is problematic and further services may be needed.
The absence of a red-reflex is abnormal. Consult with an ophthalmologist immediately.

answer:
The correct answer is D.

The absence of a red reflex indicates that there is obstruction of visual input to the retina. This is essential for normal visual pathway development in infants.

review.t: Examination of a Well Newborn & Infant

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following is a cause for concern in newborn children?

options.html: 5-10% weight loss in the first 3 days

answer:
The correct answer is E.

Torticollis occurs when the child’s neck is persistently tilted which could indicate injury to the neck muscles during birth. Caput Succedaneum involves edema of the scalp that crosses the suture lines of the skull – it is common and tends to resolve within 1-2 days. Acrocyanosis is blueness in the limbs which is common at birth and tends to resolve on its own. Mild Syndactyly where digits are fused together at their origin are common. Newborns normally lose 5-10% of their weight in the first 1-3 days of life but return to birth weight by day 7-10.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: You are performing a newborn examination. Which observation is the most concerning?

options.html: Nose exam: absence of choanal atresia
Groin area exam: Presence of meconium
Eye exam: Presence of white eye reflex
Upper Extremity: Presence of double palmar crease

answer:
The correct answer is D.

In a newborn exam, a healthy reflex is the red reflex. A white reflex indicates obstruction of light to the retina. Choanal atresia is a blocking of the nasal passages; Meconium is the name for the first stool passed, and its absence may indicate an imperforate anus. Colobomas are missingtissues in the iris of the eye. More concerning than a double palmar crease is a single palmar crease, which may indicate a chromosomal abnormality.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which option below correctly describes a finger abnormality?
answer:
The correct answer is A.

Polydactyly refers to extra fingers, clinodactyly refers to curved fingers, and brachydactyly refers to short fingers. Tachydactyly is a made-up term.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following is a sign of abnormal development in children?

options.html: A child is not sitting by 9 months
Hand still fisted at 1 month of age
A child not able to walk independently at 1 year old
A child is fearful of strangers at 6 months

answer:
The correct answer is A.

Children are usually able to sit independently at 6 months old, however if they don’t develop this ability by 9 months of age this is abnormal. Children normally develop stranger anxiety at 6 months of age. Hands that are fisted are not a concern until 4 months of age. While children are able to walk independently at 1 year of age, it is not classified as abnormal development unless it persists for 1.5 years.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem:
With regard to growth charts which of the following is indicative of failure to thrive?

  1. Weight trajectory crosses 2 major percentile lines in the downward direction
  2. Height less than 3%ile (not a family norm)
  3. Weight less than 10%ile
answer:
The correct answer is A.

Weight less than 3%ile (and it is not the family norm) is considered failure to thrive.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following statements are correct?

options.html: Binocular vision and language development both have a critical period of development in infancy
Binocular vision and language development both have a sensitive period of development in infancy
Binocular vision has a critical period of development in infancy and Language Development has a sensitive period of development in infancy
Binocular vision has a sensitive period of development in infancy and Language Development has a critical period of development in infancy

answer:
The correct answer is C.

A critical period requires stimuli during that period, or else you will develop a deficit that can’t be reversed. A sensitive period is a window of opportunity where it is easiest for a skill to be learned or developed, however you can still develop this later on. Binocular vision has a critical period early in life and language development has a sensitive period in infancy (adults can learn new languages but it’s much harder for them.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A 12-month-old child does not experience any distress when the parent leaves their presence for extended periods of time. The mother discourages the infant crying and responds infrequently when the child is distressed. Which of the following attachment styles best describe this parent-child relationship?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

The insecure-avoidant attachment style is characterized by children who don’t actively seek out their parents when separated (treat them similar to strangers) and this can be due to a lack of response from the parent when the child is distressed or discouraging crying/comfort from the infant.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following best exemplifies the Transactional model for Parent infant relationships?

options.html: Parents speak in a high voice to their infant, the infant registers high voices better and smiles, the mother sees the smile and continues to speak in a high voice
The parent speaks to their child in a high-pitched voice as they know from parenting classes that children will benefit from this
The parent has an innate desire to speak in a high-pitched voice to their child which is beneficial to the child’s development
The parent and child have an implicit agreement where the parent will provide comfort for the child in exchange for motherly/fatherly bonding

answer:
The correct answer is A.

In the transactional model a parent and child’s behaviors are shaped by each other’s responses over time. In the example a parent continues to speak in a high-pitched voice after seeing the baby’s smile.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: In which of the following Piaget’s stages do children make imaginary friends and draw them?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

In the preoperational stage, children are capable of symbolic play and use language and drawings to represent their experience.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A mother comes in with her 18-month-old child who is not using single words at this point. After taking a comprehensive history which of the following is the next best step?

options.html: Encourage the parent to wait, as children do not use single words until they are 2 years old
Ask the parent to read to their children as this promotes language development within the child
Examine the child’s vocal cords and oral cavity

answer:
The correct answer is C.

A child who is not meeting their language milestones, might point towards a hearing impairment as hearing and speaking go hand-in-hand in promoting language development. A hearing impairment is important to rule out before reaching other conclusions.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: You are assessing a child for developmental age. She can roll from supine to prone and prefer their caregivers to strangers. What is the developmental age?
answer:
The correct answer is C.

Rolling from supine to prone, as well as preferring caregivers are key developmental milestones of a 6-month old.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: You are assessing a child for developmental age. He knows 10-25 words, including “mine”, and likes to pretend talk on the phone. What is the developmental age?
answer:
The correct answer is C.

Children begin to talk at about 12 months, but at 18 months, they should know 10-25 words.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: You are assessing a 5-year-old child for developmental age. She can partake in pretend play and has just started taking part in back and forth communication and describing what others may be thinking. What is her developmental quotient?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

Back-and-forth communication starts with 36-month-olds (3 years), as does pretend play and some empathetic/social skills such as describing what others are thinking. Since the child is 5 years old, the developmental quotient would be 0.6 (3/5).

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which option explains the observation that females who are genetic carriers of an X[1]linked recessive condition may demonstrate some symptoms of the condition?

options.html: X-linked is only ever dominant; never recessive.
Haploinsufficiency is a mechanism by which only one functional copy of a normal allele does not provide enough protein for adequate functioning
Recessive-negative means that the improper functioning of the defective protein also has a deleterious effect on neighbouring, wildtype proteins
Anticipation: This occurs when parents anticipate the gene defects and associated conditions in their offspring and demonstrate the symptoms themselves.
X-inactivation during fetal development means that in all cells, one of the X[1]chromosomes is silenced at random.

answer:
The correct answer is E.

One copy of each X-chromosome is silenced during embryonic development. If the “normal” copy of a gene on the X-chromosome is silenced, the other X-chromosome containing the mutated gene will be expressed.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which option does not explain the presence of Down syndrome in the offspring of two parents?

options.html: Robertsonian translocation der(14,21)(p1;p1) in the mother
Robertsonian translocation der(14,21)(q10;q10) in the father
De novo nondisjunction during mitosis after fertilization

answer:
The correct answer is A.

There is no P arm for chromosomes 14 and 21 because they are acrocentric.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A low risk patient pays out of pocket for Non-Invasive Prenatal Testing that screens positive for Trisomy 21. Which of the following are the next best steps?

options.html: Refer the patient for a Fetal Anatomy Scan to examine congenital abnormalities associated with Trisomy 21
Refer the patient for Amniocentesis or Chorionic Villi Sampling to confirm Trisomy 21
Refer the patient for a Nuchal Translucency to confirm Trisomy 21
Provide the patient with additional Folic Acid

answer:
The correct answer is B.

NIPT is considered a screening test, thus a patient would need an invasive diagnostic test (either Amniocentesis or Chorionic Villi Sampling) to confirm their diagnosis. Both the Fetal Anatomy Scan and Nuchal Translucency are screening tests. Folic Acid helps with the prevention of neural tube defects; however this would not help in this scenario.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which statement below concerning prenatal screen for chromosomal abnormalities is false?

options.html: Nuchal translucency is an ultrasound technique that measures the thickness of fluid at the back of the neck.
Fetal anatomy scans are ultrasound scans that can be used to determine the baby’s sex, as well as to look for neural tube defects and heart defects
Enhanced First trimester screening (eFTS) combines both Nuchal translucency ultrasound and first trimester maternal serum screening
Non-invasive prenatal testing is a diagnostic technique for Down syndrome involving fetal free DNA being leaked into the maternal bloodstream.

answer:
The correct answer is D.

This answer is mostly true, but NIPT is not a diagnostic tool; this is a screening tool. If NIPT is positive, additional diagnostic techniques are available (amniocentesis, chorionic villi sampling) for diagnosis.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A patient of yours who is 10 weeks pregnant and concerned about chromosomal abnormalities in her child wants to do invasive prenatal testing. To ensure your patient has informed consent, what should you ensure she understands before ordering tests?

options.html: Chorionic villi sampling is a very safe procedure and can be performed as early as next week.
Amniocentesis involves taking a sample of the mother’s blood and can be performed in about one month.
There is an inherent risk of miscarriage involved for any invasive prenatal test.
Chorionic villi sampling and amniocentesis are not considered diagnostic.
All of the above should be mentioned

answer:
The correct answer is C.

Chorionic villi sampling has an associated risk of miscarriage of 1/100. Amniocentesis involves taking a sample of amniotic fluid with a risk of miscarriage of 1/200. Both of these are considered diagnostic for chromosomal abnormalities.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.

preamble.title: Shared instructions
preamble.html:
The following stem applies to the following 2 question:

Mr. and Mrs. Smith, who have recently found out that they are pregnant, visit a genetic

counsellor to discuss a genetic condition that runs in both of their families. After taking a family

history, you draw their family pedigree, as shown. Use the pedigree to answer the next TWO

questions.

stem: Analyze the above pedigree. Which statement below is true?

options.html: Mrs. Smith’s niece died at the age of 6 months.
One or Mr. Smith’s nieces was adopted into the family.
Mrs. Smith’s father was affected and passed away from the condition in his 60’s.

answer:
The correct answer is B.

A is incorrect - Mrs. Smith’s niece was still-born at 6 months gestation. C is incorrect – his niece is affected. D is incorrect - while Mrs. Smith’s father passed away in his 60’s, he did not have the condition.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Analyze the pedigree above to deduce the mode of inheritance (autosomal dominant, autosomal recessive, X-linked). ASSUME 100% PENETRANCE. What is the probability that Mr. and Mrs. Smith’s child will be affected by the condition?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

The inheritance pattern is autosomal recessive, since the condition can appear “spontaneously”. It cannot be X-linked recessive, or else individual 6 would necessarily be affected. Since both Mr. and Mrs. Smith have at least one affected parent, they must both be carriers of the condition. This means their child has a 25% chance (½ * ½) of having the condition.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A newborn with suspected Down syndrome has undergone QF-PCR confirming the diagnosis. What is the next most probable investigation?

options.html: Microarray to confirm the diagnosis of Down syndrome and assess for other chromosomal abnormalities
FISH to check for DiGeorge syndrome
Karyotype to understand the specific nature of this case of Down syndrome
Microarray to assess for balanced translocations
Gene sequence to find out if the extra chromosome came from mom or dad

answer:
The correct answer is C.

After the diagnosis of Down syndrome by QF-PCR, a karyotype allows for the microscopic analysis of chromosomes to determine the nature of the condition: Either aneuploidic trisomy 21, Robertsonian trisomy 21 or mosaic trisomy 21.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following correctly matches the chromosomal abnormality with its common name?
answer:
The correct answer is D.

Patients with Turner’s syndrome have a single X-chromosome. Trisomy 18 is Edward syndrome; XXY is Klinefelter syndrome; Trisomy 13 is Patau syndrome; and Trisomy 21 is Down syndrome. DiGeorge syndrome is associated with a microdeletion on chromosome 22.

weekLabel: Week 4 - Child & Adolescent Health, Immunity & Vaccines
lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following compounds are found in breast milk in meaningful quantities? Choose as many as applicable.
answer:
The correct answer is A, C, E.

Vitamin D and Iron are not found in meaningful quantities in breast milk. Breastfed infants require supplemental Vitamin D to make requirements. Infants have iron stores to last the first 6 months of life after which point they require iron rich solid food.

weekLabel: Week 4 - Child & Adolescent Health, Immunity & Vaccines
lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A new mother comes in with her 1-month old infant and explains how her infant requires (cries) to be fed every 2-3 hours. What is an appropriate response to her concern?

options.html: Explain how the infants should be fed on demand which is usually every 2-3 hours, the infant's behavior is normal
Suggest developing a scheduled routine so the baby is breastfed at convenient times in the day
Suggest switching to concentrate as this may be more filling for the infant
Explain how infants typically cry as attention seeking behavior and this should not be continually addressed

answer:
The correct answer is A.

Infants should be fed on demand, which is typically every 2-3 hours.

weekLabel: Week 4 - Child & Adolescent Health, Immunity & Vaccines
lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: You are assessing a six-month-old boy while discussing his eating habits with the mother. Which one statement by the mother gives you the most concern?

options.html: The mother coaxes her baby to eat pablum by sweetening it with honey.
The mother will keep breastfeeding her baby in addition to providing lumpy solid foods.
The mother is concerned about infections since her child brings objects to his mouth.
The mother intends to start feeding her baby crushed peanuts soon.

answer:
The correct answer is A.

Infants younger than 1 year old should not be fed honey. At this age, infants are at risk of botulism poisoning which affects the nervous system

weekLabel: Week 4 - Child & Adolescent Health, Immunity & Vaccines
lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A 4-year-old child is having severe separation anxiety from her parents and has difficulty with social interactions. With regards to readiness for school which factor does this fall under?
answer:
The correct answer is C.

Emotional readiness for school involves being able to tolerate separation from parents and make friends.

weekLabel: Week 4 - Child & Adolescent Health, Immunity & Vaccines
lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Taylor is a healthy child who is entering Grade 2. At this grade what is a realistic goal for Taylor’s learning?

options.html: Taylor is able to begin to use her reading skills to learn new topics.
Taylor is building her reading and math skills.
Taylor is able to work on abstract projects.
Taylor is able to work in groups.

answer:
The correct answer is B.

In grade 1-2, children begin learning the fundamentals of reading, writing and mathematics. In grade 3-4 children switch from learning to read to reading to learn. In junior and senior kindergarten children begin working in groups. In grade 5-6 Taylor is expected to understand abstract concepts.

weekLabel: Week 4 - Child & Adolescent Health, Immunity & Vaccines
lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: When is dyslexia likely to be diagnosed?
answer:
The correct answer is D.

In Grades 1/2, education focuses on learning to read. It’s not until grade 3/4 where education focuses on reading to learn - at this point, conditions like dyslexia are most likely to be noticed.

weekLabel: Week 4 - Child & Adolescent Health, Immunity & Vaccines
lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A mother comes in with her 4 year old child, who she describes is having an excessive amount of temper tantrums. After taking an extensive history you learn the child has a significant global developmental delay, and is often unable to articulate their thoughts. There are no unexplained injuries or concerns. Which of the following is the next best step?

options.html: Make a referral for an investigation to the Children’s Aid Society as excessive anger can point to abuse.
Speak with the child individually to determine if they are a victim of abuse.
Perform a physical exam to see hidden causes of discomfort.
Explain to the mother how temper tantrums are normal for a child that is four years old.

answer:
The correct answer is C.

Children who cannot articulate their thoughts may not be able to articulate discomfort and pain in their body, so a detailed physical exam should be conducted to examine this. The stem does not suggest the child is a victim of abuse and although temper tantrums are fairly normal the mother’s concern should not be dismissed.

weekLabel: Week 4 - Child & Adolescent Health, Immunity & Vaccines
lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A mother comes in with her 6 month old infant, who she says is waking up and crying frequently throughout the night. What advice is appropriate in this scenario?

options.html: The mother should attend to the infant, however should make the interactions short.
The mother should not attend to the infant, so the infant can resume sleeping.
The mother should sleep with the infant in the same bed to provide ongoing comfort.
The mother should discourage the infant from crying at night.

answer:
The correct answer is A.

The mother should attend the baby to provide reassurance but make the interactions short. The mother should not sleep with the child in the same bed as turning over at night could injure/kill the child.

weekLabel: Week 4 - Child & Adolescent Health, Immunity & Vaccines
lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.

preamble.title: Shared instructions
preamble.html: The next two questions are based on the same clinical scenario.

stem: Taylor’s family is unable to afford the school materials she needs for fifth grade. Consequently, she does poorly in school, loses interest and is more likely to drop out by the time she reaches high school. What phenomenon pertaining to the social determinants of health does this situation best describe?
answer:
The correct answer is C.

Pathways is a sequence of exposures in one stage of life which increase the likelihood of other exposures occurring later in life. Accumulation is a series of multiple exposures which combine to a have a significant effect. Latency is at exposure in one point in your life having a direct effect years later in your life.

weekLabel: Week 4 - Child & Adolescent Health, Immunity & Vaccines
lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Taylor is at risk of dropping out of high school and it is believed her family’s poverty in childhood contributed to this. Which of the following represents an upstream intervention relevant to this scenario?

options.html: A program designed for students at risk of dropping out, to help them get back on track
A program aimed at raising the minimum wage so all parents can afford the necessities of their children
A program aimed at helping low-income families with young children
A program aimed at helping students who have dropped out of high school get their high school diploma

answer:
The correct answer is B.

This is an example of an upstream intervention as it aims at diminishing the root cause (poverty) behind dropping out of school - raising minimum wage reduces poverty which reduces dropping out. Upstream interventions also occur at a national level and seek to reform social and economic structures that distribute wealth, power, opportunities, and decision-making.

weekLabel: Week 4 - Child & Adolescent Health, Immunity & Vaccines
lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following phrases explain the differentiation between impairment and disability?

options.html: A person is disabled by their illness but chooses to be impaired
A person is impaired by their illness but chooses to be disabled
A person is disabled by their illness but impaired by society
A person is impaired by their illness but disabled by society

answer:
The correct answer is E.

Impairment is the loss or limitation of physical mental or sensory function on a long- term/permanent basis. Disability is the loss of the ability to take part in normal life of the community due to physical and social barriers in their community.

weekLabel: Week 4 - Child & Adolescent Health, Immunity & Vaccines
lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A 6-month-old baby boy is brought to a family clinic by his mother. Because of COVID, the mother has been able to work from home and have her baby with her throughout the day. Her work does not involve Zoom, so she can readily breast-feed him when he is hungry, even while she is working. He is not receiving any other supplements. During the physical examination, the physician notes a soft skull, frontal bossing (protruding forehead) and epiphyseal enlargement. A deficiency in which of the following best explains this presentation?
answer:
The correct answer is D.

Vitamin D deficiency presents as craniotabes (soft, thin skull), frontal bossing, rachitic rosary and epiphyseal enlargement. The baby is kept indoors during the day and is exclusively breastfed with no other supplements, so a Vitamin D deficiency explains the baby’s presentation.

weekLabel: Week 4 - Child & Adolescent Health, Immunity & Vaccines
lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following laboratory assessments is appropriate to test for an iron deficiency in infants?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

Ferritin is the best screening test, serum iron should be reserved for iron overload evaluation or complex iron assessments.

weekLabel: Week 4 - Child & Adolescent Health, Immunity & Vaccines
lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A 10 year old child is repeatedly sent to detention for distracting the class, getting up and walking around, and not being able to pay attention in class. Otherwise the child has no further concerns and is generally doing well. The mother is concerned the child has ADHD. Based on the current information does the child fit the diagnostic criteria for ADHD?

options.html: No, the symptoms must present before the age of 6
No, the symptoms must be present in two or more settings
No, the symptoms do not reduce the quality of functioning for this child
Yes, the child meets the diagnostic criteria

answer:
The correct answer is B.

The symptoms must be present in two or more settings to meet the diagnostic criteria for ADHD, and these symptoms only seem to be present at school. Some symptoms must be present before 12 years old (age criterion). The symptoms do clearly interfere with the child’s academic functioning.

weekLabel: Week 4 - Child & Adolescent Health, Immunity & Vaccines
lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following attributes is NOT involved in the etiology of ADHD?
answer:
The correct answer is D.

Parenting is not a cause but can influence the management of ADHD.

weekLabel: Week 4 - Child & Adolescent Health, Immunity & Vaccines
lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which is not required to make a diagnosis of ADHD?

options.html: Symptoms of inattention must persist for more than 6 months
Symptoms of inattention are present in two or more settings
Clear evidence that symptoms interfere with functioning
Symptoms are not better explained by another disorder

answer:
The correct answer is A.

Symptoms of ADHD can be observed, and the condition diagnosed, before the age of 12. The remaining options are from the DSM-5 for diagnosing ADHD.

weekLabel: Week 4 - Child & Adolescent Health, Immunity & Vaccines
lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem:
According to the Tanner stages for boys, in what order do the following typically occur?

  1. Scrotum and testes have grown
  2. The penis has grown in length and width
  3. Pubic hair extends upwards to the umbilicus
answer:
The correct answer is A.

Testicular growth occurs first, followed by penis enlargement, and lastly pubic hair growth. However, there can be some overlap between these stages.

weekLabel: Week 4 - Child & Adolescent Health, Immunity & Vaccines
lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: During which stage of psychosexual development do youth tend to focus more on exploring intimacy with others and sexuality, including masturbation?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

Middle adolescence is associated with experimenting in sexual roles, masturbation, exploring intimacy in others and forming crushes. Early adolescence is associated with “hero worship” and developing crushes on others. Late adolescence is associated with intimacy and multifaceted relationships, long-term planning, family planning and accepting imperfections in others.

weekLabel: Week 4 - Child & Adolescent Health, Immunity & Vaccines
lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following explains the phenomena of a 16-year-old immigrant from Syria rejecting her Syrian heritage and being rejected from Canadian culture?
answer:
The correct answer is D.

Marginalization involves rejecting the receiving and heritage culture. Integration involves accepting the receiving culture and their heritage culture. Assimilation involves accepting the receiving culture and rejecting their heritage culture. Separation involves rejecting their receiving culture and maintain their heritage culture.

weekLabel: Week 4 - Child & Adolescent Health, Immunity & Vaccines
lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: You are seeing a 16-year-old patient and asking questions to screen their risk of alcohol abuse. Which question below is NOT part of the CRAFFT questionnaire?

options.html: Do you ever use alcohol while you are alone?
Have you ever gotten into trouble while using alcohol?
Do you feel annoyed when your family or friends ask you to cut down on alcohol use?
Do you ever use alcohol to relax, feel better about yourself, or fit in?
Have you ever ridden in a car driven by someone (including yourself) who was drunk?

answer:
The correct answer is C.

This question asked in Option C is part of the CAGE questionnaire for alcohol abuse: “Do you get annoyed when people ask about/criticize your drinking?” The remaining two questions in the CRAFFT questionnaire are “Do you ever forget things you did while using alcohol or drugs?”, and “Do your family or friends ever tell you that you should cut down on your drinking or drug use?”

weekLabel: Week 4 - Child & Adolescent Health, Immunity & Vaccines
lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Below are several descriptions of acculturation of recently immigrated persons to Canada. Which description is correctly matched with an acculturation style?

options.html: A 15-year-old Iranian immigrant chooses to completely reject her Iranian culture and adapt to Canadian culture. This is an example of Assimilation.
A 47-year-old Chinese immigrant maintains his heritage culture but refuses to adapt to Canadian culture. This is an example of Marginalization.

A 22-year-old Mexican immigrant no longer relates to his family and friends back at home, and due to his immigrant status cannot form meaningful relationships with Canadians. This is an example of Separation.
A 35-year-old Irish immigrant celebrates Canadian culture at the expense of her heritage culture. This is an example of Integration.

answer:
The correct answer is A.

This is an example of assimilation. Option B is an example of separation. Option C is an example of marginalization. Option D is another example of assimilation. The last category is integration, where the heritage culture is retained and the receiving culture is accepted.

weekLabel: Week 4 - Child & Adolescent Health, Immunity & Vaccines
lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: There are several different theories of cognitive development. Antonio is a 12-year-old boy who has recently started going through puberty. Which statement below on the theories of cognitive development is true?

options.html: According to Freud, Antonio’s current psychosexual stage is the genital stage where his primary drives are towards intercourse and adult sexuality.
According to Piaget’s theory of cognitive development, Antonio’s current stage is Formal operations. He is now capable of hypotheticodeductive reasoning.
According to Erikson’s psychosocial theory, Antonio’s current crisis is identity vs. role confusion. He is likely attempting to establish his identity and his role in society.

answer:
The correct answer is E.

An adolescent would normally be in Freud’s genital stage, Piaget’s Formal Operations stage, and Erikson’s identity vs. role confusion stage.

lectureMeta: Written fresh by the Meds 2025 volunteers (December 2021). The bank states on its own second page that these were not verified by faculty.
stem: A 13-year-old girl presents to the clinic with general fatigue and a loss of sleep in the past week. How would you characterize her symptoms?
answer:
The correct answer is C.

Fatigue and sleep loss are undifferentiated symptoms that are not specific to one body system. Her symptoms also present over the past week, so it’s acute (chronic symptoms usually take months to develop).

lectureMeta: Written fresh by the Meds 2025 volunteers (December 2021). The bank states on its own second page that these were not verified by faculty.
stem: A patient comes to the clinic with a severe rash, what is this presentation?
answer:
The correct answer is C.

From 01 - Introduction to MCC Clinical Presentations. A symptom is what the patient perceives as not normal and complains of; a sign is objective evidence the practitioner observes or elicits on examination. A severe rash is both: the patient notices it and comes in because of it, and the clinician can see and describe it.

  • A or B alone is incomplete - each captures only one side of the finding.
  • D fails: a diagnosis identifies the underlying illness (burn, poisoning); “rash” is a finding that still needs a differential.

stem: Which one of the following falls under the proximal factors of health
answer:
The correct answer is B.

From 02 - Tasks of a Physician 1 - Patient-Centered Approach. The patient-centred method splits context in two. Proximal context is generally modifiable and directly influences illness: family, education, employment, social supports, financial security. Distal context is non-modifiable and acts indirectly: culture, community, faith/beliefs, ecosystem, society.

  • A (faith/beliefs), C (culture) and D (society) are all distal.
  • E fails because it pairs a distal factor (faith) with employment.

options.html: Exploring both diseases and illness experience

options.html: Don’t recommend tests in anticipation of preceptor preference
Seek clarification if you suspect something is ordered unnecessarily
Consider the most diagnostic test first
Only order test that will change patient management

answer:
The correct answer is C.

One should consider ordering the least invasive test first, which may or may not be the most diagnostic.

lectureMeta: Written fresh by the Meds 2025 volunteers (December 2021). The bank states on its own second page that these were not verified by faculty.
stem: Which of the following is false regarding imaging modalities:

options.html: X-rays image the body based on tissue density
MRI allows great contrast between soft tissues
Ultrasound is a form of dynamic imaging that uses the doppler effect

answer:
The correct answer is D.

Bones appear white on radiographs.

From 10 - Body System Organization (Week 2), which holds the imaging material. The question asks for the false statement. The lecture's density table runs air (black) → water (charcoal) → soft tissue (grey) → bone (white) → metal (white with beam hardening), so bone appearing grey is false.

  • A true: radiographs separate structures by tissue opacity (silhouetting), which follows density.
  • B true: MRI weighting (T1 for fat, T2 for fluid, proton density for cartilage and tendon) distinguishes soft tissues x-ray cannot.
  • C true: ultrasound uses high-frequency sound in real time; the Doppler detail is not in the note but is standard.

stem: Kay has a family history of high blood pressure. Her diet consists of many fatty foods. She was recently diagnosed with hypertension. She had also recently lost her job shortly after her diagnosis. Due to the shortage of income, she was choosing cheaper food options that are usually prepackaged and high in sodium. What is the impact of her loss of job and subsequent diet options on her health?
answer:
The correct answer is A.

Perpetuating factors maintain the problem once it is established. In this case, her job loss after her diagnosis is leading her to make more unhealthy diet options that exacerbates her hypertension.

lectureMeta: Written fresh by the Meds 2025 volunteers (December 2021). The bank states on its own second page that these were not verified by faculty.
stem: Which of the following is true regarding chronic stress

options.html: The chronic hyperactivity of the arousal system could be a source of long-term biological damage
The body releases high levels of ADH and cortisol during stress
Chronic stress is associated with weight gain

answer:
The correct answer is D.

ADH is not produced during stress, but cortisol is.

Chronic stress keeps the arousal system (sympathetic and HPA axis) switched on. That sustained activation is itself a source of long-term biological damage (A), and chronic cortisol exposure promotes appetite, central fat deposition and weight gain (C). So the key is D, “A and C”, and it rules out B.

The bank's reason for excluding B is that ADH is not produced during stress. That is questionable (see the flag). A safer reading is that B is wrong as a blanket “high levels of ADH and cortisol” claim, so E (“all of the above”) falls with it.

stem: Which one of the following correctly describes a stage in epidemiologic transition

options.html: Pestilence and famine: the lowest life expectancy with a majority of death attributing to cardiovascular diseases
Receding pandemics: there is improved nutrition and public health measures which leads to reduction in infectious disease, but people still don’t live long enough to experience chronic diseases
Degenerative and man-made diseases: chronic diseases overtake infectious disease and a little less than half of deaths can be attribute to cardiovascular diseases
Delayed degenerative diseases: cardiovascular and cancer are the leading cause of death

The correct answer is D.

From 06 - Introduction to Epidemiology & Population Health.   • B fails: in receding pandemics people do live long enough (to about 50) to experience chronic disease.
  • C: the lecture describes this stage as chronic disease overtaking infection with CVD at under 50% of deaths - see the flag.

stem: Racism and colonization are intertwined and together deeply impact the health of Indigenous people in Canada.
answer:
The correct answer is A.

From 10 - Cultural Competence in Health Care and the Care of Refugees. The lecture's cultural competence continuum places forced assimilation and subjugation (cultural destructiveness) and racism (cultural incapacity) at its lowest stages, and grounds cultural safety in self-determination and decolonization - a concept first defined because of poor health outcomes in the colonized Maori people. Colonization is the historical system and racism the ongoing practice that sustains it, so they act together on Indigenous health, which is why decolonizing care is offered as the remedy.

stem: Which of the following colonial polices and practices should be recognized when understanding Indigenous Health?

options.html: Past and present child welfare process

answer:
The correct answer is E.

All four are colonial policies and practices whose effects on Indigenous health persist, so E.

  • A: the Indian Act (1876) imposed federal control over First Nations identity, governance and land, and is still in force.
  • B: forced relocation of Inuit communities (the High Arctic relocations of the 1950s) broke ties to land and livelihood.
  • C: the residential school system removed children from families and culture, with abuse and intergenerational trauma.
  • D: child welfare, past (the Sixties Scoop) and present (overrepresentation of Indigenous children in care), continues that separation.

The course's cultural safety material ties this together: cultural safety rests on self-determination and de-colonization.

stem: Which of the following is FALSE regarding enzyme activity and kinetics?

options.html: Enzymes provide the activation energy for a reaction to occur.

Enzymatic activity does not change the required reactants or the end products of a reaction.

answer:
The correct answer is A.

Enzymes lower the activation energy if a reaction

From 01 - Biochemistry. The note states that the main function of enzymes is to lower activation energy. They do not supply it, so A is the false statement.

  • B is true word for word: enzymes facilitate a reaction that could happen on its own but does not, or happens very slowly.

  • D is true on the note: higher substrate concentration means faster product formation, which is why a disease with little (or poorly binding) enzyme can be treated by raising the substrate to make use of the enzyme that is present.

stem:
Match the following types of blinding to the appropriate definition:

  1. Open Label
  2. Single Blind
  3. Double Blind
  4. Triple Blind

options.html: either the patient or clinician unaware of treatment allocation

answer:
A – III; B – I; C – IV; D – II.

From 10 - Body System Organization. Each level of blinding hides allocation from one more party (stem order: I open label, II single, III double, IV triple):

  • Open label (I) = all parties aware → B.
  • Single blind (II) = the patient or the clinician is unaware → D.
  • Double blind (III) = both patient and investigator unaware → A.
  • Triple blind (IV) = patient, investigator and the analysts unaware → C.

12 - Evidence-Based Medicine adds why it matters: blinding reduces performance and detection bias, and is critical when the outcome is subjective, less so when it is objective.

stem:
Match the following description to the appropriate type of connective tissue

  1. Loose Connective Tissue
  2. Dense irregular connective tissue
  3. Reticular connective tissue
  4. Dense regular connective tissue

options.html: Found in the reticular layer of the dermis and most organ capsules (resilient and protective)
Found in tendons, ligaments, joint capsules and has high stress resistance
Found in hematopoietic tissues such as bone marrow, lymph nodes and spleen
Poorly organized fibers found under epithelia, carrying vessels and nerves

answer:
A – II; B – IV; C – III; D – I.

From 06 - Connective Tissue. Taking the terms as I loose, II dense irregular, III reticular, IV dense regular (the order the stem lists them), the keyed mapping matches the note's table exactly.

  • A – II: dense irregular CT is found in most organ capsules and the reticular layer of the dermis; its type I and III collagen is woven into a mat, making it resilient and protective.
  • B – IV: dense regular CT (tendons, ligaments, joint capsules) has fibroblasts and type I collagen in rows, for high stress resistance.
  • C – III: reticular CT (type III collagen from reticular cells) supports the hematopoietic tissues: marrow, lymph nodes, spleen.
  • D – I: loose CT sits under epithelia, carries vessels and nerves, and has poorly organized fibres.

stem:
Match the following descriptions to either:

  1. White Adipose Tissue
  2. Brown Adipose Tissue

options.html: Thermoregulation and energy storage for newborns
Expands up to 4x its size before dividing

answer:
I – C, D, G, H; II – A, B, E, F.

From 06 - Connective Tissue. With I = white and II = brown adipose tissue:

  • White (C, D, G, H): the adult energy store and insulator; unilocular (one lipid vacuole per cell), which pushes the nucleus to the periphery; the cells can grow about 4× before dividing, and once divided are hard to clear.
  • Brown (A, B, E, F): abundant in newborns (2-5% of body weight) for thermoregulation; multilocular (many small droplets), so the nucleus stays central; packed with mitochondria, which is what makes it a heat generator.

The discriminator is locularity: one droplet displaces the nucleus, many droplets leave it central.

Match the following bone cell types to its description

From 06 - Connective Tissue. The four bone cells form a lineage plus one outsider.

  • A marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells = osteoprogenitor cells (III), in the periosteum and endosteum, which differentiate into osteoblasts during repair.

  • D multinucleated cells that resorb matrix = osteoclasts (I), the outsider, fused from blood monocytes/macrophages rather than the mesenchymal line.

stem: What would happen to cells when placed in a hypotonic solution?
answer:
The correct answer is C.

From 02 - Osmosis. Tonicity is a solution's ability to cause water movement. A hypotonic solution (about 200 mOsm/kg against the cell's ~300) has less solute outside than inside, so water is drawn into the cell by osmosis and it swells (the note's mnemonic: the ‘O’ in hypOtonic means the cell expands).

  • A (no change) describes an isotonic solution, where there is no net water movement.
  • B (shrink) describes a hypertonic solution, which pulls water out of the cell.

stem: What is the correct sequence of events in an action potential?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

From 08 - Cellular Communication. The note's sequence: a graded depolarization reaches threshold (about −55 mV); voltage-gated Na+ channels open and the membrane depolarizes rapidly to about +45 mV; Na+ channels inactivate and K+ rushes out, repolarizing it toward −70 mV; the slow K+ channels stay open too long, so it hyperpolarizes (undershoot) before the Na+/K+ pump restores rest.

  • A puts repolarization before depolarization; there is nothing to repolarize from yet.
  • C starts with repolarization and ends with depolarization, the reverse of the cycle.
  • D swaps the last two: the undershoot follows repolarization, it does not precede it.

stem: Which of the following is the correct sequence of events of Excitation Contraction Coupling?

options.html: Voltage propagation down T-Tubules → Release of Calcium from SR → Myosin attachment to actin → Calcium binding to Troponin → Actin slides over Myosin
Release of Calcium from SR → Voltage propagation down T-tubules → Myosin attachment to actin → Calcium binding to Troponin → Actin slides over Myosin
Voltage propagation down T-Tubules → Release of Calcium from SR → Calcium binding to Troponin → Myosin attachment to actin → Actin slides over Myosin
Release of Calcium from SR → Voltage propagation down T-tubules → Calcium binding to Troponin → Myosin attachment to actin → Actin slides over Myosin

answer:
The correct answer is C.

From 05 - Muscle Tissue. Excitation-contraction coupling runs electrical → chemical → mechanical:

  • The action potential spreads down the T-tubules (inward folds of the sarcolemma).
  • This makes the sarcoplasmic reticulum release Ca2+ from its terminal cisternae (the triad).
  • Ca2+ binds troponin C, shifting tropomyosin off the myosin-binding sites.
  • Only then can myosin bind actin and perform the power stroke, so actin slides over myosin and the I band and H zone shorten.

A puts myosin binding before calcium-troponin binding, impossible while tropomyosin blocks the sites. B and D release calcium before the voltage reaches the SR, reversing cause and effect.

stem: Which of the following is FALSE about conventional radiography?

options.html: The amount of radiation is considered low risk for non-contraindicated patients.

answer:
The correct answer is C.

A minimum of 2 is needed.

From 10 - Body System Organization. The lecture's radiograph rules answer every option. A structure needs a minimum of 2 radiographs at 90° to one another (e.g. AP/PA plus lateral), because one 2D view suffers from summation, where overlapping structures mimic an abnormality. Four is not the minimum, so C is the false statement.

  • A true: plain films use ionizing radiation, but CT is the modality the lecture singles out for a much larger dose.
  • B true: a radiograph is a 2D projection, unlike CT's slices.
  • D true: air is least dense and appears black; bone and metal appear white.

lectureMeta: Written fresh by the Meds 2025 volunteers (December 2021). The bank states on its own second page that these were not verified by faculty.
stem: What mode of inheritance does this pedigree show?
answer:
The correct answer is C.

X linked recessive

From 02 - Genetics. Affected individuals are almost all male, and the pattern follows the X. The affected mother (1) has both sons affected and her daughters (4, 6) unaffected, which fits carrier daughters. Carrier daughter 4 with an unaffected partner has one affected son (9), and all her daughters are unaffected: the note's “female carriers to sons”. Affected son 7 married to an affected woman (8) has all children affected, as expected when the mother has two variant X's.

  • A (AD) fails because unaffected 4 has an affected son (a skipped generation).
  • B (AR) would need unrelated partners 2 and 3 both to be carriers, and would not favour males.
  • D (new dominant) fails because the grandmother is already affected, so nothing arose de novo.

The figure is printed mirror-reversed, so the numbers read backwards.

stem: What is the risk of down syndrome in a mother who is 38?
answer:
The correct answer is C.

From 05 - Genetic Screening, as far as it goes. The lecture says Down syndrome risk rises with maternal age, uses 1:350 as the eFTS cut-off, and funds NIPT from age 40. The usual age-related figures run roughly 1:350 at 35, rising to about 1:175 around 38 and 1:100 at 40, so a 38-year-old sits between 1:175 and 1:100 (C).

  • A 1:900-1:600 is the risk of women around 30 or younger.
  • B 1:350-1:175 covers 35-37.
  • D greater than 1:100 applies from about 40 onward.

The logic to remember: the risk roughly doubles every 2-3 years after 35.

stem: What is the Nipissing (LookSee) test?

options.html: It is comprised of a short list of yes or no questions about the child’s abilities.

Can diagnose a child with a developmental disorder

answer:
The correct answer is D.

Options A and B are correct.

From 01 - Child Development and 08 - Developmental Milestones. The Nipissing (LookSee) checklist is a parent-completed questionnaire of yes/no questions about what the child can do, reviewed by the physician. One “no” is a positive screen, and it is very sensitive but not very specific. It is used repeatedly at well-child visits across early childhood (Nipissing Plus adds photos for less literate parents).

  • A true: short yes/no list about abilities.
  • B true: it tracks development over the early years at each visit.
  • C false: it is a screening tool; a positive screen leads to assessment, and only assessment diagnoses.

So D (A and B).

stem: An example of an upstream intervention would be:

Heart and Stroke Foundation, an international non-profit organization, campaigning for increased physical activity in schools

= iii, B = i, C = ii, D = i. NK cells are involved in both innate and adaptive immune responses. PRRs and PAMPs are innate immune mechanisms. T-cells require antigen presentation and are therefore part of the adaptive immune response. Tissue resident cells include macrophages and sentinel cells – they are both part of the innate immune response.

stem: Which of the following inaccurately describes the corresponding type of vaccine?

options.html: Live attenuated vaccines – generate longer-lasting and broader immunity than killed vaccines.
Non-live vaccines – immune response is mostly humoral and antibody titre will diminish over time.
Live attenuated vaccines – pre-existing circulating antibody enhances the immune response induced by vaccination.
Subunit vaccines – polysaccharide vaccines are not immunogenic in children under 2 years of age.

answer:
The correct answer is C.

Circulating antibody interferes with the immune response elicited by live attenuated vaccines. All other statements are correct.

stem: Conjugate vaccines have drastically reduced the incidence of meningitis and pneumonia. All of the following are properties of conjugate vaccines EXCEPT:

options.html: Ability to induce an immune response in children younger than 2 years old.
Persistence of protection against the given pathogen.
Generation of a T-cell dependent immune response.
Hyporesponsiveness/immune tolerance of the given pathogen.

answer:
The correct answer is E.

Hyporesponsiveness/immune tolerance is occasionally observed in polysaccharide vaccines such as HiB and meningococcus C. This is not an issue with conjugate vaccines.

stem: In which of the following scenarios would pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) be the most clinically indicated and beneficial?

options.html: A nurse sustains a needle-stick injury from a contaminated needle.
A male neonate is delivered vaginally; his mother has HIV.
An immunosuppressed woman was exposed to Varicella zoster virus at work.
A patient is planning to become sexually active with their new partner who is HIV positive.

answer:
The correct answer is D.

This patient is vulnerable to sexually transmitted HIV infection. Since the high-risk activity can be anticipated, pre-exposure chemoprophylaxis is indicated and can prevent HIV infection. The people in the other answers would all benefit from post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP).

stem: Which of the following incorrectly describes one of Piaget’s Theories of Development?

options.html: Concrete operations – some logical thought processes such as inversibility and single viewpoints
Formal operations – can reason logically and think about things abstractly such as metaphors, analogies, and self-reflection
Sensorimotor – learning occurs through exploration and manipulation of the environment, and object permanence is achieved
Preoperational – capable of symbolic representations in play, and there is a decline in egocentricity

answer:
The correct answer is A.

The concrete operations stage is characterized by logical thought processes like reversibility (the ability to see things from multiple perspectives; inversibility is a made-up term for the purposes of this question), as well as conservation (volume of liquid does not change even if shape of container does).

stem: Which of the following correctly orders Piaget’s Theories of Development? Birth-2y → 2-7y → 7-11y → 12+y

options.html: Preoperational → sensorimotor → formal operations → concrete operations
Sensorimotor → preoperational → formal operations → concrete operations
Sensorimotor → preoperational → concrete operations → formal operations
Preoperational → concrete operations → formal operations → sensorimotor

answer:
The correct answer is C.

From 04 - School Age. Piaget's stages in the note's order: sensorimotor (0-2) – learning through activity, object permanence; preoperational (2-7) – symbolic representation and play; concrete operational (7-11) – conservation, reversibility, classifying by more than one quality; formal operational (12+) – abstract and hypothetical reasoning (C).

  • A and D start with preoperational, but object permanence and sensorimotor learning come first.
  • B puts formal before concrete; logical thought about concrete objects precedes abstract thought.

Physicians play a key role in assessing child readiness for school by monitoring developmental milestones, vision, and hearing
Delaying school entry is not recommended because it puts the child one year behind their peers and negatively influences their development
In middle childhood, growth tends to be slower than in preschool years but occurs in spurts

If a child is determined not to be ready for school, delaying school entry is a strategy that can be used. Assess whether the behaviour is consistent with the child’s developmental age

If a child’s behaviour is determined to be atypical this requires further assessment and treatment. Anticipatory guidance is provided to parents at each well child visit to help them understand what typical behaviours they should expect to see and prepare for between visits.

stem: There are many common behaviours in children and infants that can cause stress and anxiety in parents. Which of the following does NOT describe an appropriate response to the behaviour?

options.html: Temper tantrums – provide resources to parents for behaviour management if tantrums are excessive and/or not appropriate for child’s developmental level
Non-compliance (e.g., not cleaning room) – evaluate whether the expectations are appropriate for age and developmental stage
Night waking – provide activities for infants until the infant is able to fall back asleep
Colic – evaluate for causes of discomfort and reassure parents
Headbanging – distract infant with other activities and give them

answer:
The correct answer is C.

The most important intervention for night waking is to promote good sleep hygiene. This can be done by setting a bedtime, enforcing it, and having a quiet and consistent bedtime routine. During a night wake, it is best to reassure the infant but provide minimal stimulation in order to help them get back to sleep.

stem: A man presents to the ER with large dark purple marks on his skin suggesting massive internal bleeding. On further questioning, he reports he was struck by a motorcycle downtown.
answer:
The correct answer is C.

Classic example of mechanical trauma.

From 02 - Tasks of a Physician 1 - Patient-Centered Approach. VITAMIN C&D classifies by cause, and the cause here is a motorcycle striking him: the T of VITAMIN, traumatic/toxic (C). The bruising and internal bleeding are the result, not the category.

  • A (vascular) is the tempting distractor, since bleeding involves vessels, but vascular means a primary vessel problem such as an aneurysm or infarct, not a vessel torn by impact.
  • B, D, E: nothing infectious, autoimmune or metabolic is suggested.
  • F, G, H, I: no medical intervention, tumour, congenital lesion or degeneration explains an acute injury after a collision.

stem: At the end plate, an end-plate potential leads to an action potential. When the action potential is initiated, which of the listed channels/pumps is responsible for the depolarization phase of the action potential?
answer:
The correct answer is A.

Acetylcholine reaches the end plate and binds to nicotinic receptors which opens chemically gated channels. This allows sodium to flow into the muscle cell and potassium to flow out. The exchange of ions leads to depolarization of the end plate called the end-plate potential (EPP). When this EPP is strong enough to reach threshold and trigger an action potential, Na+ voltage-gated channels open causing the remaining depolarization of the action potential.

stem: Which of the listed channels/pumps is responsible for ending the contraction of a muscle?
answer:
The correct answer is G.

Calcium binds to troponin causing tropomyosin to roll of myosin binding sites found on actin. This allows myosin to attach to acting forming a crossbridge and allowing the power stroke to occur. The actin slides over the myosin causing the muscle to contract. Ca2+ is actively pumped back into the sarcoplasmic reticulum by the Ca2+ ATPase pump. When Ca2+ is removed, tropomyosin covers myosin binding sites and allows the muscle to relax, ending the contraction phase.

stem: You are out enjoying a lovely summer’s day by having a picnic beside a forest. A hungry bear smells the tasty food that you have spent so much time preparing and comes lumbering toward you. You see the bear and you switch from a parasympathetic dominant state to a sympathetic dominant state. What is the body focused on doing now? Choose the 4 most correct answers.

options.html: Dilates blood vessels to skeletal muscle

answer:
The correct answer is C, E, G, H.

The parasympathetic nervous system is commonly thought of as the “rest and digest” system. It is involved with lacrimation (tears), salivation, urination, digestion, defecation, and sexual arousal. On the other hand, the sympathetic nervous system is commonly thought of as the “fight or flight” system. It is involved with dilation of pupils, bronchioles, and blood vessels to skeletal muscle. It increases heart rate and contraction. It constricts blood vessels to the GI organs to slow digestion. To further slow digestion, it decreases GI peristalsis. Sweat secretion is also activated by the sympathetic nervous system. Thus, your body switches from eating and enjoying your picnic to focusing on getting away from the bear.

stem: The venous blood from the intestine proceeds through which vessel first?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

Portal vein is where GI system’s venous return goes.

From 03 - Body Systems Integration (Week 5). All venous blood leaving the GI tract enters the portal system, draining through the portal vein to the liver before it reaches the systemic veins: absorbed nutrients → portal system → liver → caval system → IVC → right atrium.

  • A IVC is later still: it receives the hepatic veins.
  • D SVC drains the head, neck and upper limbs, not the gut.

The first-pass route through the liver is why the order matters.

Bathing, dressing, and grooming are IADLs; meal preparation and grocery shopping are ADLs.

stem: A 55-year-old woman presents to her healthcare provider with complaints of lower back pain that has persisted for several months. She reports that the pain is worse in the morning and improves with movement throughout the day. She also reports that the pain is exacerbated by prolonged sitting. Based on this scenario, which of the following is an example of a perpetuating factor for the patient's pain?

options.html: The pain is worse in the morning.
The pain is exacerbated by prolonged sitting.
The patient is 55 years old. Levels of Prevention

answer: C) The pain is exacerbated by prolonged sitting. Perpetuating factors are factors that contribute to the maintenance of a condition or symptom over time. The patient's lower back pain is being perpetuated by prolonged sitting, which exacerbates the pain. This perpetuating factor can lead to a vicious cycle where the patient avoids sitting, which can lead to deconditioning and further perpetuation of the pain. Pain worse in the morning is a temporal pattern. Pain that improves with movement is an example of a relieving factor and not a perpetuating factor. Patient age is not a perpetuating factor for the patient's pain.

stem: Osteogenesis Imperfecta (OI) is an autosomal dominant disorder affecting Type 1 collagen and may have a mild or severe presentation. Choose the answer below that best explains why this occurs.

options.html: In mild OI a mutant protein is produced that affects the function of the normal protein, termed a dominant negative effect.
In mild OI a single functioning allele of a gene is not sufficient to produce a normal phenotype, termed haploinsufficiency.
In severe OI a mutant protein is produced that affects the function of the normal protein, termed a dominant negative effect.
In severe OI a single functioning allele of a gene is not sufficient to produce a normal phenotype, termed haploinsufficiency.

answer:
The correct answer is E.

Mild OI is due to a null mutation leading to a truncated protein that cannot participate in collagen formation and is degraded (haploinsufficiency). Severe OI is due to the inclusion of mutated alpha chains into the collagen molecule, affecting the overall coiling of collagen (dominant negative effect).

stem: Which of the following lists the ACMG categories of genetic variants from least significant to most significant?

options.html: benign, likely benign, variant of uncertain significance, likely pathogenic, pathogenic
benign, likely benign, likely pathogenic, variant of uncertain significance, pathogenic
likely benign, benign, likely pathogenic, variant of uncertain significance, pathogenic
benign, likely benign, likely pathogenic, pathogenic, variant of uncertain significance

answer:
The correct answer is A.

The American College of Medical Genetics uses a five tier system to classify genetic variants: Benign - This variant is known to not cause disease. Likely benign - This variant is not expected to cause disease, but information is inconclusive. Uncertain significance - there is not enough information to support a more definitive classification of this variant. Likely pathogenic - there is a high likelihood (>90% certainty) that this variant is disease-causing. Pathogenic - this variant directly contributes to the development of disease. Note that some pathogenic variants may not be fully penetrant, or may not be sufficient to cause disease on their own (recessive, x-linked)

stem: Ms. McConnel comes into your office with her 2 year old daughter, Maeve. She is concerned with the development of Maeve’s fine motor skills. She explains that her Maeve’s older sibling has been previously diagnosed with a developmental delay, and she is worried that Maeve is exhibiting similar delays. What is the most appropriate next step to take?

options.html: Use the Rourke Baby Record to score Maeve’s developmental progression
Tell Ms. McConnel that it is too early to tell if Maeve’s fine motor skills are delayed, and that you will follow up at her next well child check up
Immediately send Maeve for further assessment so that she can be diagnosed with a developmental delay
Send Ms. McConnel home with an Ages and Stages Questionnaire and plan a follow up appointment for when it is completed

answer:
The correct answer is D.

A-The Rourke Baby Record is a form of developmental surveillance, appropriate for healthy, low risk infants. Because Maeve is exhibiting concerning delays, it is not the appropriate choice. B-It is important to carefully monitor developmental milestones and investigate concerns because early intervention shows the best outcomes. C-Children should not be sent for further assessment without a positive developmental screen that has focused in on the area of concern. D-This is the correct answer. The Ages and Stages Questionnaire is a developmental screening tool used to identify children from 1 month to 5.5 years that would benefit from in-depth evaluation. Ms. McConnel can complete this at home and its results will inform further decisions about Maeve’s care.

stem: A couple are expecting a child and decide to complete genetic testing on the child. Through the testing, it is discovered that the child has Uniparental disomy of paternal origin. What does this mean for the child?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

A)This is incorrect. The child’s sex does not have an influence on the outcome of this particular finding. It is the sex of the parent responsible for the disomy that will determine whether the child will experience B or C. B) This is the correct answer. UPD15 is short form for uni-parental disomy of chromosome 15. Because the disomy is from the father of the child, the child will have Angelman Syndrome. This is because the chromosome has a gene called UBE3A, the paternal form of which is inactive in certain parts of the brain, leading to the development of Angelman Syndrome. C) This is incorrect. If the UPD15 was of maternal origin, this would be the outcome. However, since the UPD15 is of paternal origin, B is correct. D) Patau Syndrome is also known as Trisomy 13. This is when the child has three copies of chromosome 13. It does not involve chromosome 15 in any way and therefore is not the correct answer. E) This is incorrect. UPD15 indicates a uni-parental disomy of chromosome 15. Depending on the origin of the UPD15, the child will either have Angelman Syndrome or Prader-Willi Syndrome.

stem: Which of the listed options is incorrect with regards to the Division of Responsibility (DOR) in terms of child nutrition?

options.html: DOR is contraindicated in children who have active eating disorders, larger bodies, and certain medical conditions that impact appetite.
Parents are responsible for what, when, and where to eat.
DOR focuses on the feeding relationship rather than nutrient intake.
Children are responsible for whether and how much to eat.
DOR emphasizes the provision and not the deprivation of food.

answer:
The correct answer is A.

A) This is the correct answer. DOR is contraindicated in children with certain medical conditions that impact appetite and who have active eating disorders, especially early in the treatment stage. B) In the DOR model, parents are responsible for what, when, and where to eat. C) DOR does focus on the feeding relationship rather than nutrient intake. D) In the DOR model, children are responsible for whether and how much to eat. E) DOR does emphasize that children should be provided with ample food rather than deprived of it with some nutritional/caloric goal in mind.

stem: Which of the following is an incorrect statement in regards to the Weight-Inclusive Approach to Healthcare?

options.html: Appreciate that bodes naturally come in a variety of shapes and sizes.
Encourage an end-goal focus for day-to-day quality of life.
Create Healthful, individualized practices and environments that are sustainable.
Work to increase health access, autonomy, and social justice for all individuals along the entire weight spectrum.
Given that health is multidimensional, maintain a holistic focus

answer:
The correct answer is B.

A) This is a correct statement. Physicians should ensure optimal health and well-being is provided to everyone, regardless of their weight. B) This is an incorrect statement. Physicians should encourage a process-focus for day-to-day quality of life. For example, people can notice what makes their bodies rested and energetic today and incorporate that into future behaviour, but also notice if it changes; they realize that well-being is dynamic rather than fixed. They keep adjusting what they know about their changing bodies. C) This is a correct statement. Where possible, work with families, schools, and communities to provide safe physical activity resources and ways to improve access to nutrient-dense foods. D) This is a correct statement. Trust that people move toward greater health when given access to stigma-free heath care and opportunities (e.g. gyms with equipment for people of all sizes; trainers who focus on increments in strength, flexibility, VO2 Max, and pleasure rather than weight and weight loss. E) This is a correct statement. Physicians should examine a number of behavioural and modifiable health indices rather than a predominant focus on weight/weight loss.

stem: A child is currently able to understand that some aspects of life are no longer reversible such as death but does not yet understand that a volume of liquid does not change even if the shape of the container does. Which stage is the child currently in according to the Theories of Development by Piaget?
answer:
The correct answer is C.

This child is working through the concrete operations stage since they understand reversibility but not yet conservation. This puts them in the approximate age range of 7-11 years old. In this stage they will also learn to understand multiple viewpoints, classification, and sequences. A) occurs from birth to 2 years old. Here the child learns to differentiate self from world, develops ideas about events, and achieves object permanence. B) occurs from 2-7 years old. Here the child develops symbolic play, language, and drawing as a means of representing experience, and egocentricity declines. D) occurs from 12 years old and onwards. Here the child understands abstract ideas, analogies and metaphors, engages in self-reflection, and is able to manipulate variables.

stem: With consideration to the social determinants of health, which of the following terms refers to how one determinant sets up for another determinant later in life?
answer:
The correct answer is D.

A) This is not correct. Latency refers to how a current determinant will not affect an individual until later. B) This is not correct. Accumulation refers to how multiple determinants are worse combined than the sum of the individual determinants. C) This is not correct. Upstream thinking is used to find out what determinants are driving an individual’s current situation and what can be done to better it. D) This is correct. An example of this would be that exposure to domestic violence in early childhood may reduce early school success, which may affect long-term school performance, school completion and future job opportunities. E) This is not correct. ACEs are experiences in childhood that negatively affect the child’s development (physical, mental, emotional, social).
